description:
Issue summary:
Fastlane Retail experienced a production incident starting 2026-03-10 03:42 UTC where a sudden spike in control-plane retries caused a heartbeat amplification across their reserved GPU pool. This manifested as repeated session tears, truncated streaming responses, elevated 5xx rates, and unexpectedly high token billing for affected time windows.

Impact:
- ~75% of Fastlane's inference sessions in us-east-1 saw session tear or reconnect within a 22-minute window.
- Customers reported truncated completions and duplicate/replayed chunks in streaming responses.
- Billing exposure estimated at +12% token usage during the window.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) in prod-us-east
- Pool: fastlane-prod-gpu-pool-3 (A100s)
- Model variants: redwood-7b-quant-v2 (primary) with open-8k-compat fallback

Timeline (high level):
- 03:42 UTC: Spike in control-plane retries observed by autoscaler metrics.
- 03:44 UTC: First customer report to support of truncated streaming and reconnects.
- 03:46 UTC: SRE alert triggered: queue backlog + ack debt on broker.
- 03:50 UTC: Canary rollback to previous kernel profile began.
- 04:05 UTC: Temporary routing policy applied (route Fastlane to alternative pool).
- 04:20 UTC: Traffic normalized; monitoring showed decline in retries and error rate.

Steps to reproduce (investigation repro steps):
1) Replay customer traffic capture against fastlane-prod-gpu-pool-3 test cluster with same concurrency and request size distribution.
2) Inject delayed ACKs on broker to emulate backlog and observe retry amplification.
3) Run streaming session workload with continuous batching enabled and simulated network jitter.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- Broker ack backlog graphs: https://observability.redwood/s/alerts/ack-backlog/fastlane-prod-gpu-pool-3
- Serving runtime logs (sample): rtx-serving-03.log (attached to incident)
- Billing window snapshot: billing-2026-03-10-03-00-05-00.csv (internal)

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rate-limited control-plane retries and increased broker ack timeouts for the pool.
- Applied routing rule to shift 40% of traffic to fastlane-prod-gpu-pool-2 while engineers validated kernel profile rollback.
- Issued immediate billing hold and flagged customer for credit review.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: a combination of a recent kernel profile change (PR merged 2026-03-09) and transient broker queue pressure created ack debt. Ack debt led to client-side retries and a heartbeat amplification loop: retries -> more inflight requests -> scheduler backpressure -> delayed ACKs -> retries.

What we found:
- Kernel profile af3c9e7 adjusted a continuous-batching threshold that increased simultaneous KV cache allocations for 7b-quant, increasing GPU memory working set under real traffic patterns.
- Autoscaler reacted to sustained latency by scaling up pods but scaling actions caused transient rebalance and increased broker queue lengths.
- Client SDK retry policy (aggressive immediate retries for stream handshakes) amplified the transient errors into a storm.

Evidence:
- Correlation between PR deployment timestamp and first error uptick in prod.
- Broker metrics show ack latency spiked from 50ms baseline to >500ms during peak.
- Replaying traffic with the new kernel profile reproduced session tear rate increase by ~3x in staging repro cluster.

Open hypotheses (already reduced to primary cause):
1) Kernel profile change increased memory pressure under this workload and raised tail latency. (high confidence)
2) Scheduler rebalance logic lacked hysteresis during immediate scale-up and contributed to queue churn. (medium confidence)
3) Customer SDK retries had no jitter/backoff, causing amplification at control-plane level. (high confidence)
comments: 2026-03-10 04:00 - Support - Aisha Patel: Notified customer Slack channel and opened this ticket. Customer reporting intermittent truncated streams and reconnects. Escalating to SRE.

2026-03-10 04:08 - SRE - Liam O'Connor: Observed ack backlog on broker for pool fastlane-prod-gpu-pool-3. Increasing broker ack timeout and applying rate limit. Working on routing 40% traffic to pool-2.

2026-03-10 04:22 - SRE - Sofia Ruiz: After routing change error rates dropped ~78%. Initiated controlled rollback of the kernel profile that was deployed 2026-03-09. Repro consistent in staging with kernel profile active.

2026-03-10 05:10 - Engineering - Miguel Santos: Patch landed to add jittered exponential backoff to control-plane handshake retries in SDK (PR 2114). Will schedule hotfix deploy to Dedicated control plane tomorrow if postmortem action approved.

2026-03-11 09:15 - Support - Aisha Patel: Customer acceptance: Fastlane confirms restore of normal streaming behavior and accepts temporary routing mitigation. Requesting billing credit for token overage window.
2026-03-12 14:02 - SRE - Liam O'Connor: Post-incident metrics show stable ack latencies and no recurrence in 48h. Closing incident with recommended action items assigned.
2026-03-12 16:45 - Customer - Emma Chen (Fastlane SRE): Thanks team — accept credit and request delivery of full post-incident report and code changes. Will need an on-call review session next week.
2026-03-12 18:00 - Support - Aisha Patel: Noted action: schedule 30m runbook walkthrough with customer week of 2026-03-16. Billing credit process started (Finance ticket FIN-2026-0443).
resolution:
Root cause assigned to combined kernel-profile memory-pressure + aggressive client retry amplification. Resolved by: 1) Rolling back kernel profile change for the affected pools; 2) Applying control-plane retry rate-limits and increasing broker ACK timeouts; 3) Shipping SDK hotfix to add jittered exponential backoff for handshake/retry behavior (PR 2114); 4) Temporary routing to alternate pool while we validated rollback.

Follow-up actions (owners and ETA):
- Engineering (Miguel Santos): Harden kernel-profile deployment test matrix to include continuous-batching memory pressure scenarios. ETA: 2026-04-02.
- Scheduler (Liam O'Connor): Add hysteresis to scale-up rebalance and a new alert for broker ack latency >200ms. ETA: 2026-03-24.
- SDK team (Sofia Ruiz): Fast-track SDK patch rollout to dedicated control planes and publish release notes; coordinate customer upgrade. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Support (Aisha Patel): Deliver customer post-incident report and schedule runbook walkthrough. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Billing (Finance): Issue credit for confirmed overage window and report to customer. Ticket FIN-2026-0443.

Customer impact mitigation: credit issued, traffic restored, and no recurrence in 72-hour observation window. Incident marked as resolved.
notes_for_handbook: Add a checklist to Dedicated rollouts that includes: (a) memory working-set stress test with real request-size mix, (b) broker ack latency monitoring and pre-deploy thresholds, (c) client SDK retry policies compatibility verification. Assignable in runbook templates.
customer_communication_summary: We acknowledged the issue within 6 minutes of first report, applied mitigations within 10 minutes, and restored normal service within ~38 minutes. Customer accepted our temporary routing and rollback, requested billing credit which Finance is processing. A post-incident walkthrough is scheduled. Full technical report linked.
